problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=\frac{1}{(t+1)^{2}}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has a velocity $v=1$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$

Question 8
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=1(t+1)2, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has a velocity v=1 when t=0s, find the velocity (in m/s) of the particle at time t.

a
v(t)=−1t+1+1
b
v(t)=−1t+1+2
c
v(t)=2t+1
d
v(t)=1t+1
e
v(t)=−1t+1−2
Submit
